bet.text: Shoot on the move, with a turret and two intakes. Looking back, the team said these made up for some speed and stability lost to a higher center of gravity and narrower wheel base.

demand.text: Cargo: with such a low ball count, the team wanted to take in as much as it could. Its championship strategy was to stay out and shoot in the endgame, since the field is typically fairly open while other robots hang, and then come in for a mid climb.
The interviewer says the team chose to climb to high and not traversal.

auto.text: Another team's championship pit data lists five high shots in auto.

cycle.text: The driver tries to keep the static arms toward the hub and takes cargo on either side, rotating at most about 90 degrees. The indexer counts balls for the operator; wrong-color cargo goes behind the hub. In Houston the robot was always in move-and-shoot mode, and in the division and on Einstein the operator did the shooting.

endgame.text: At the championship: shoot for about 20 seconds, then a mid climb of about 3. The high climb pulls up on mid onto stationary hooks, swings the extending arm to high by piston, then pulls up half way; once disabled, the climber extends slowly enough that the robot is still up about five seconds after the match.

fallback.text: Odometry gives the position with or without the Limelight, which corrects it.
In 2023 the team said of turrets that one also helped when pinned against the wall or other robots.

gave_up.text: The team called it a bigger, slower robot than 1678's that could not consistently get open shots. With a higher center of gravity and narrower wheel base it added a significant slew rate limiter and ran lower top speed and acceleration. On average at worlds, it noted, 1678 outscored it with one intake and no turret.

changed.text: After St. Louis the team added acceleration compensation to its moving shot, and before the championship a color sensor. It said the robot needed fixing after tough Einstein matches.
Intake wheels became grip-taped tube; the climb stops half way up mid after swings caused early falls.
Off-season: one button picks the intake from robot motion, the driver shoots, and the aiming was reworked.

outcome.text: 51-6-1 in official play; won the Hopper division; captain of the Hopper alliance on Einstein; ranked 7 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 62.71, Hopper).

cost.text: A higher center of gravity and narrower wheel base forced a significant slew rate limiter and lower top speed, acceleration and deceleration

facts.text: Wheel speeds are PID controlled, which gives the robot's velocities for aiming
In the released code a keep-angle controller runs briefly after driving; the team thinks this counters rotation from quick deceleration, and stops so the robot does not keep trying while stationary
Another team's championship pit data lists length 33, width 25, height 44 and weight 124 (units not given)

solves.text: Take in as much cargo as possible in a game with a low ball count, without rotating to face each ball

cost.text: Two intake buttons plus driving left the operator to shoot; the team put most missed shots down to miscommunication or bad timing

facts.text: The most the robot ever has to rotate to pick up balls, about
Rollers are Lexan tube covered in skateboard grip tape, the entire width of the intake
In the Hopper division, two buttons deployed the intakes from the driver's perspective; some cases were hard to get perfect
Off-season: one button puts down the intake closest to the direction the robot is moving

solves.text: Index to the same precise spot every time and keep one ball from knocking another through the shooter

facts.text: A proximity sensor at the bottom detects a ball; a color sensor at the top decides where it is shot
Sensors were moved around until balls fit in and touched without moving
The ball count is sent to the operator, who then knows when to shoot

functions.name: Turret

solves.text: Shoot with a defender on the bumper, because a bigger, slower robot could not consistently get open shots

functions.type: powered turret with a dead band

facts.text: About a 20 to 30 degree dead band at the back, set by the wiring
The driver's controller rumbles when the wanted angle is in the dead zone
In 2023 the team said it had found a little more precision and speed with a turret than in rotating a whole robot to aim
An Armabot turret, as used in previous years

solves.text: Two piston positions, used in the previous two years, were not enough control

facts.text: Moves to any degree under PID control
In March a team post said it could shoot from almost anywhere, slightly less accurately farther out

solves.text: Too much backspin made the ball roll after it hit

facts.text: Small upper wheels deaden the ball so it does not roll back too far
Shooter speed is PID controlled
By the team's own count, 33 scored and 4 missed in teleop of one match
Another scouting group's data also has 33, with 10 in the last 20 seconds
Another team's championship pit data lists a turreted multi-flywheel shooter and five high shots in auto

solves.text: Without acceleration in the sum, turret, hood and shooter lagged whenever the robot started or stopped

cost.text: At St. Louis, before the factor, a stationary shot had to wait for the turret, and the team hardly used the mode

facts.text: The goal is shifted by the ball's flight time multiplied by robot velocity plus acceleration times a factor; turret, hood and flywheel then aim at that virtual goal
The shot is the same as a stationary shot from the virtual goal's distance, from tables of hood and speed
The acceleration factor was found by experiment: how fast the robot will be moving in about
At times it could shoot while moving at over
For 0.1 s after the color sensor sees a wrong ball, the target switches to another point
Off-season: the virtual goal is recalculated up to five times until the flight time settles
A 2025 post says the system approached 1690's level, especially at IRI

solves.text: Know position while moving, even with the target at the edge of the image

facts.text: Distance, gyro, turret angle and target offset give a pose when the target is valid
A lookup table gave better results than a straight trigonometric approach for this game
July 2022 code lowered the vertical angle by the horizontal angle divided by 12, since an off-center target makes the robot look closer

Off-season (August): data at four distances, turning the turret about 5 degrees at a time, gave a function that replaced that correction, so one table of vertical angle against distance works off center

functions.name: Climber

solves.text: Pulling up on mid too high or too fast made the robot swing and caused a couple of early falls

functions.type: three-stage telescoping climber with stationary hooks

facts.text: Machined in house from an existing design
Stationary hooks release when the match starts and hold the robot on mid while the arm, moved by piston, reaches high
It stops half way up mid so the back of the robot drags and slows the swing
High takes probably about 12 seconds to pull up, after leaving about 3 seconds early to get there; asked how long it takes, the team says it usually goes at about 15 to 20
A commenter said on 10 April that none of that year's St. Louis winners, 1706 among them, could climb traversal
On high it pulls up only half way: pulling onto the stationary hooks sometimes made the bumper hit the mid bar and the robot fall off

decisions.because: the ball count is low, and one intake would mean rotating before each pickup

decisions.choice: A turret on a swerve drive
decisions.because: looking back, a bigger, slower robot probably needed to shoot with a defender on its bumper

decisions.choice: A hood that moves to any degree
decisions.because: two set positions were not enough control
decisions.instead_of: a piston hood with two positions

decisions.choice: Grip tape on a tube for the intake roller
decisions.because: the ball bounced weirdly off separate rubber wheels
decisions.instead_of: black rubber wheels on a hex shaft

decisions.choice: Shoot wrong-color cargo behind the hub
decisions.instead_of: choosing the spot by robot position

decisions.choice: Add acceleration compensation to the moving shot
decisions.because: the turret, hood and shooter lagged when starting and stopping
a straight trigonometric approach gave poor results for this game

decisions.choice: Stay out and shoot in the endgame, then a mid climb
decisions.because: the field is typically fairly open while other robots hang
the driver knows exactly when to move smoothly, and one person needs less reaction time
decisions.instead_of: the operator shooting, as in the division and on Einstein

decisions.because: the team felt defense would be hard to program around
